player_action: I made my Will save against the enchanter's spell. Do I know what she tried to cast?
game_state: PC succeeds Will save vs an enchantment with no obvious physical effect.
correct_ruling: A creature that successfully saves against a spell without obvious physical effects feels a hostile force or a tingle, but can't deduce the exact nature of the attack. He knows something was tried, not which spell.
srd_reference: MagicOverview.rtf > Saving Throw > Succeeding on a Saving Throw

player_action: Can I identify the spell the enemy cast on me while it's being cast?
game_state: Wizard with Spellcraft watching an enemy cast at him.
correct_ruling: Yes, by rules: identifying a spell as it's being cast is a Spellcraft check (DC 15 + spell level) and requires seeing or hearing the components. What the DM narrates beyond that (e.g., recognizing the caster's tradition) is DM discretion.
common_wrong_rulings: No way to identify spells as cast.

player_action: The trap in this homebrew dungeon has no save listed. It just says 'darts shoot out'. Do I get a Reflex save?
game_state: DM's own trap description lists an attack bonus but no save.
correct_ruling: Traps in the SRD either make an attack roll or allow a save, as specified. If the trap is written as an attack, there's no save; if the description is incomplete, the DM decides, and should pick one mechanic (attack roll vs AC or Reflex save), not both.
common_wrong_rulings: Every trap always allows a Reflex save.
Attack roll and then a save for half.
confidence_note: SRD trap stat blocks specify either attack bonus or save DC; the 'pick one' guidance is a judgment summary, not a quote.

player_action: I'm holding the door shut against a creature using a spell that forces me back. Does my strength help?
game_state: Ambiguous: a homebrew 'force push' effect, no save type specified by the module author.
correct_ruling: The rules don't cover this unspecified effect; the DM decides the mechanic. A defensible ruling is to map it to the nearest SRD mechanic (e.g., a bull-rush-style opposed Strength check or a Fortitude/Reflex save) and apply it consistently.
common_wrong_rulings: Inventing a specific RAW rule and citing it.

player_action: My elf is targeted by sleep. I get my +2 against enchantments, right?
game_state: Elf PC targeted by sleep spell.
correct_ruling: Better: elves are immune to magic sleep effects, so sleep has no effect at all. The +2 racial bonus applies to saves against other enchantment spells and effects.

player_action: I'm the target of a fireball and also get Reflex saves from my ring; I want to roll twice and take the better.
game_state: No ability granting a reroll; ring of protection +1 (deflection to AC only).
correct_ruling: There's no general 'roll twice take the better' mechanic in 3.5 absent a specific ability. He rolls one Reflex save; a ring of protection adds deflection to AC, not to saves.
srd_reference: MagicItems > Rings > Protection; CombatI.rtf > Saving Throws
common_wrong_rulings: Ring of protection adds to saves.

player_action: The DC is too high, it's unfair. Other DMs let you reroll a failed save with a hero point. Let me reroll.
game_state: Core SRD game with no action/hero point variant in use.
correct_ruling: Core SRD 3.5 has no hero/action point rerolls; the failed save stands unless a specific ability grants a reroll. The DM could adopt a variant, but that isn't RAW.

player_action: My character is a hardened soldier; mind-affecting stuff shouldn't work on him. I don't need to roll vs the charm.
game_state: Human fighter targeted by charm person.
correct_ruling: Character concept doesn't grant immunity. He makes a Will save as normal (with his Will bonus and any applicable bonuses); on a failure he is charmed.

player_action: Massive damage is an optional rule, everyone knows that. Skip the save.
game_state: PC took 55 damage from a single attack; table uses core SRD.
correct_ruling: Massive damage is part of the core SRD combat rules (DC 15 Fortitude save or die), not an optional variant. Unless the table has explicitly house-ruled it out, he must make the save.
srd_reference: CombatI.rtf > Injury and Death > Massive Damage
common_wrong_rulings: Agreeing it is optional and skipping it.
Converting to 5e instant-death at negative max hp.

player_action: Does the dragon know I'm going to roll a save? Can I fake failing my save against its charm to trick it?
game_state: PC wants to succeed on the save but act as if charmed.
correct_ruling: The save is rolled normally; the rules don't govern pretending afterward. Pretending to be charmed is roleplay; the DM decides whether the dragon notices (a Bluff vs Sense Motive check is a reasonable mechanic).
common_wrong_rulings: Pretending is impossible because the caster knows.

player_action: The treant is hit by my sleep spell. Will save?
correct_ruling: Plants are immune to sleep effects (as well as mind-affecting effects, poison, paralysis, polymorph, and stunning), and sleep also only affects low-HD creatures. No effect.
common_wrong_rulings: Treants fall asleep in winter only.
